verses.1: They were shamed and disgraced; the people were not honored at all.
verses.2: Before you break the law, before that day comes, God will not come to you. Before that day arrives, God will not be present with you.
verses.3: Ask Jehovah for all the people of the earth. Their judgments are righteous. Ask for justice, even if they hide themselves on the day of Jehovah’s judgment.
verses.4: For Azah will be left behind, and Ashkloon will be thrown into the sky. They will drive her away, and Ekeron will be exiled.
verses.5: O you who dwell in the land of the sea! You are like a people who have not obeyed the words of Jehovah. You are like the people of Canaan, who live in the land of Philistia. But you will be destroyed by those who do not obey Jehovah.
verses.6: And the sea would become a river of poisonous creatures and venomous snakes.
verses.7: And it shall be a sign for the rest of the house of Israel: they will be like those who live in Ashkelon. In the evening, they will become numerous, but Jehovah, their God, will deal them a terrible blow, and they will be destroyed.
verses.8: I heard the shame of Moab’s people, and the insults they suffered from the children of Ammon. They humiliated my people, and they increased their suffering along their borders.
verses.9: Therefore, let the Lord, the God of Israel, have mercy on us. For Kishdom will be destroyed, and the children of Ammon will be like Amorah. They will be destroyed by fire and salt. They will be destroyed forever. My people will be destroyed, and other nations will be conquered.
verses.10: This is given to them as a reward for their suffering. They have been humiliated, but they have also risen up in defense of the people of Jehovah’s army.
verses.11: The LORD will shine upon them, for He has despised all the gods of the earth. No one from any place will be able to stand against Him; all the nations will tremble before Him.
verses.12: You also are like those who are cursed and doomed to destruction.
verses.13: And he will lay his hand on the sky, and destroy Ashur. He will also set Nebukadnezar on fire like a straw mat.
verses.14: And in her midst, there were many people who lived there throughout their entire lives. They were both men and women. Their voices echoed throughout the valley during the time of destruction. For Arzah was a beautiful woman.
verses.15: This is the beautiful city that stands firmly on its own ground. It says in its walls, “I and Ephsi still remember how it once was—a place full of life. All around it, there’s only peace and tranquility.”
